summary: Aermotor fire tower in McCurtain County, OK. Sources date it 1930s to 1953; a March 2025 forestry service post lists it closed, and its observer retired in 2016.

facts.design: Aermotor tower with a 7x7 ft cab
facts.agency: Ouachita National Forest / Oklahoma Forestry Services

staffing.status: closed; forest tower observer retired in 2016

access.note: Oklahoma Forestry Services lists the status as Closed in a March 2025 post. No source says whether visitors may approach or climb the tower.

events.note: Land Utilization Project agreement (OK-LU-24) dated October 15, 1952. The land is now owned by the Ouachita National Forest.
Forestry service gives 1953 as the year the tower was erected; the house was built the same year.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on July 28, 2009.
Forest tower observer retired in 2016, according to the forestry service.

corrections.current: Quachita National Forest / Oklahoma Forestry Service
corrections.proposed: Ouachita National Forest / Oklahoma Forestry Services
corrections.why: Quachita is a misspelling of Ouachita. The register and the forestry service both use the correct spelling.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's description says the 1930s, and its own record says 1950. Central Uplands says the 1930s with no exact date. The forestry service gives 1953 for erection and a 1952 land agreement. The story uses the forestry service's dates and reports the others.
The register and Central Uplands give 100 feet (30.5 m), which is the value in facts. The forestry service gives 110 feet of galvanized steel. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates (33.9053, -94.5221) match the forestry service's latitude and longitude exactly. The register's listed longitude (W 091 deg 33.000') would put the tower in Arkansas and looks like a typo for 094. Ground elevation also differs: register 167 ft, forestry service 520 ft. No source checked says plainly whether the tower still stands. No photo added.
